title: Evolution Evidence and Life History Review Test
description: Review practice for fossils, common ancestry, and evidence-based evolutionary reasoning.

questions.prompt: What does the fossil record provide evidence about?
questions.questionText: What does the fossil record provide evidence about?
options: past life and changes in organisms over time
how organisms choose traits instantly
why all rocks contain DNA
why every species is unchanged forever
questions.correctAnswer: past life and changes in organisms over time
questions.explanation: Fossils preserve clues about organisms that lived in the past.

questions.prompt: A fossil is found in a deeper rock layer than another fossil. What is often a reasonable first inference?
questions.questionText: A fossil is found in a deeper rock layer than another fossil. What is often a reasonable first inference?
options: The deeper fossil must be alive now.
The deeper fossil may be older, depending on the rock history.
The deeper fossil has no scientific value.
Depth always shows the fossil is younger.
questions.correctAnswer: The deeper fossil may be older, depending on the rock history.
questions.explanation: Relative rock layers can help scientists infer age patterns when the layers are undisturbed.

questions.prompt: Which evidence can support common ancestry?
questions.questionText: Which evidence can support common ancestry?
options: different classroom labels
the color of a notebook
similar bone patterns in different organisms
one animal being larger than another
questions.correctAnswer: similar bone patterns in different organisms
questions.explanation: Shared structural patterns can be evidence that organisms share ancestry.

questions.prompt: A whale flipper, bat wing, and human arm have similar bone arrangements. Which claim does this evidence support?
questions.questionText: A whale flipper, bat wing, and human arm have similar bone arrangements. Which claim does this evidence support?
options: The organisms are the same species.
Bones are not useful evidence.
All three structures have identical functions.
These organisms may share common ancestry.
questions.correctAnswer: These organisms may share common ancestry.
questions.explanation: Similar underlying structures with different functions can suggest common ancestry.

questions.prompt: Which model best represents evidence for life changing over time?
questions.questionText: Which model best represents evidence for life changing over time?
options: older fossils -> transitional patterns -> newer fossils
newer fossils -> no past life -> no evidence
one fossil -> every answer
organism choice -> instant fossil
questions.correctAnswer: older fossils -> transitional patterns -> newer fossils
questions.explanation: Patterns across older and newer fossils can show change over time.

questions.prompt: A student says, "One fossil proves the whole history of a group." What is the best correction?
questions.questionText: A student says, "One fossil proves the whole history of a group." What is the best correction?
options: One fossil always proves every detail.
Scientists look for patterns across many fossils and other evidence.
Fossils cannot be compared.
Evidence from rocks is never useful.
questions.correctAnswer: Scientists look for patterns across many fossils and other evidence.
questions.explanation: Strong scientific explanations use multiple lines of evidence.

questions.prompt: A rock layer contains marine shell fossils in a desert region. What claim can this support?
questions.questionText: A rock layer contains marine shell fossils in a desert region. What claim can this support?
options: Shells prove the desert is underwater today.
Fossils cannot show past environments.
The environment in that area may have been different in the past.
The shells must be plastic.
questions.correctAnswer: The environment in that area may have been different in the past.
questions.explanation: Marine fossils can show that the past environment differed from today.

questions.prompt: Which evidence would best support that two species are closely related?
questions.questionText: Which evidence would best support that two species are closely related?
options: different names in a textbook
one species living farther north
one species being photographed first
similar DNA patterns and similar body structures
questions.correctAnswer: similar DNA patterns and similar body structures
questions.explanation: Multiple shared evidence patterns strengthen a relatedness claim.

questions.prompt: A diagram compares DNA sequence patterns from several vertebrates and shows many shared sections. What can this evidence help support?
questions.questionText: A diagram compares DNA sequence patterns from several vertebrates and shows many shared sections. What can this evidence help support?
options: relatedness patterns among organisms
that all adult organisms are identical
that DNA evidence is a rock layer
that DNA patterns never vary
questions.explanation: DNA similarities can be one line of evidence for relatedness.

questions.prompt: Which statement best distinguishes a fossil from a living organism?
questions.questionText: Which statement best distinguishes a fossil from a living organism?
options: A fossil is always currently alive.
A fossil is preserved evidence of past life, not the living organism itself.
A fossil is a type of weather.
A fossil cannot be evidence.
questions.correctAnswer: A fossil is preserved evidence of past life, not the living organism itself.
questions.explanation: Fossils preserve traces or remains of past organisms.

questions.prompt: A sequence of horse fossils shows gradual changes in toe structure across rock layers. Which claim is best supported?
questions.questionText: A sequence of horse fossils shows gradual changes in toe structure across rock layers. Which claim is best supported?
options: Every individual horse changed its toes during life.
Fossils show no patterns.
Some body structures changed in that lineage over time.
Rock layers are unrelated to time.
questions.correctAnswer: Some body structures changed in that lineage over time.
questions.explanation: A fossil sequence can show population-level changes across long time spans.

questions.prompt: Which data pattern best supports common ancestry among three organisms?
questions.questionText: Which data pattern best supports common ancestry among three organisms?
options: They live in three different habitats.
They are drawn on the same page.
They have different adult sizes.
They share many DNA similarities and a similar limb-bone pattern.
questions.correctAnswer: They share many DNA similarities and a similar limb-bone pattern.
questions.explanation: Independent similarities in DNA and anatomy can support common ancestry.

questions.prompt: A student says, "Similar function always means common ancestry." Which example shows why that is too simple?
questions.questionText: A student says, "Similar function always means common ancestry." Which example shows why that is too simple?
options: Bird wings and insect wings both fly but have very different structures.
All wings are drawn with arrows.
Birds have feathers.
Insects are small.
questions.correctAnswer: Bird wings and insect wings both fly but have very different structures.
questions.explanation: Similar function alone is weaker than similar underlying structure and other evidence.

questions.prompt: Why do scientists compare fossils with modern organisms?
questions.questionText: Why do scientists compare fossils with modern organisms?
options: to avoid using evidence
to identify patterns of similarity, difference, and change over time
to prove all organisms are identical
to turn fossils into living organisms
questions.correctAnswer: to identify patterns of similarity, difference, and change over time
questions.explanation: Comparisons help connect past and present life.

questions.prompt: Which fossil discovery would most improve a model of transition between two groups?
questions.questionText: Which fossil discovery would most improve a model of transition between two groups?
options: a rock with no preserved structures
a fossil from an unknown layer with no details
a fossil with a mix of traits found in older and newer groups
a drawing with no measurements
questions.correctAnswer: a fossil with a mix of traits found in older and newer groups
questions.explanation: A fossil with mixed traits can help fill a gap in a change-over-time model.
